verses.text: I wish you would put up with me in a little foolishness. Actually, you already are.
I'm jealous for you with a godly jealousy. I promised you to one husband, to present you to Christ as a pure bride.
But I'm afraid that, just as the serpent tricked Eve with his cunning, your minds may somehow be led away from sincere devotion to Christ.
If someone comes preaching a different Jesus from the one we preached, or you receive a different spirit or a different message of good news, you put up with it easily enough.
I don't think I'm in the least inferior to those so-called super-apostles.
Even if I'm not a trained speaker, I do have knowledge. We've made that clear to you in every way.
Did I sin by lowering myself so you could be lifted up, when I shared God's Good News with you free of charge?
I accepted support from other churches, in effect taking their wages so I could serve you.
When I was with you and needed help, I wasn't a burden to anyone. The brothers who came from Macedonia supplied what I needed. I kept from burdening you in every way, and I'll keep doing so.
As surely as Christ's truth is in me, no one in Achaia will stop me from boasting about this.
Why? Because I don't love you? God knows I do.
I'll keep doing what I've been doing so I can cut off the opportunity of those who want a chance to claim their work is just like ours.
People like that are false apostles, dishonest workers who disguise themselves as apostles of Christ.
And that's no surprise. Even Satan disguises himself as an angel of light.
So it's no surprise if his servants disguise themselves as servants of righteousness. Their end will match what they've done.
I'll say it again: don't think I'm foolish. But if you do, then accept me as a fool so I can brag a little too.
What I'm saying in this confident boasting isn't something the Lord would say; I'm speaking like a fool.
Since many people brag according to human standards, I'll brag too.
You put up with fools gladly because you think you're so wise!
You put up with anyone who enslaves you, takes advantage of you, exploits you, acts superior, or slaps you in the face.
To my shame, we were too weak for that! But if anyone dares to brag—and I'm speaking foolishly—I dare too.
Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they Abraham's descendants? So am I.
Are they servants of Christ? (I'm out of my mind to talk like this.) I'm even more so: I've worked harder, been imprisoned more often, been beaten far more, and faced death again and again.
Five times I received from the Jews the forty lashes minus one.
Three times I was beaten with rods. Once I was stoned. Three times I was shipwrecked. I spent a night and a day adrift at sea.
I've been on many journeys and faced dangers from rivers, robbers, my own people, Gentiles, the city, the wilderness, the sea, and false believers.
I've worked hard and struggled, stayed awake many nights, gone hungry and thirsty, often gone without food, and been cold and without proper clothing.
Besides everything else, every day I carry the burden of concern for all the churches.
Who is weak without my feeling weak too? Who is led into sin without my burning with concern?
If I have to brag, I'll brag about the things that show my weakness.
God, the Father of the Lord Jesus, who is praised forever, knows I'm not lying.
In Damascus, the governor under King Aretas guarded the city to arrest me.
But I was lowered in a basket through a window in the wall, and escaped his hands.
